study_identification_part.si4_title: Comprehensive volumetric phenotyping of the neonatal brain in Down syndrome

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its research objectives and the purpose of applying normative modeling. (1) Research hypotheses/questions are provided: The study aimed to conduct the first detailed regional volumetric analysis of the neonatal brain in Down syndrome (DS) and quantify deviation from the normative mean in neonates with DS. (2) The purpose of applying normative modeling is explicitly described: to enable individual inference of volumetric deviation from the normative mean for a given sex, age at scan, and age from birth, allowing for the assessment of phenotypic severity at the neonatal stage which may help guide early interventions. Both criteria are satisfied.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: In this study, we aimed to conduct the first detailed regional volumetric analysis of the neonatal brain in DS. We used a robust cross-sectional sample of 493 preterm- to term-born control neonates from the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) to perform normative modeling of regional brain tissue volumes from 32 to 46 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA) at scan. Deviation from the normative mean was quantified in 25 neonates with DS from the Early Brain Imaging in DS (eBiDS) study, accounting for sex, age at scan, and age from birth variables. [...] In future, the ability to assess phenotypic severity at the neonatal stage may help guide early interventions and, ultimately, help improve neurodevelopmental outcomes in children with DS.

All three criteria are satisfied: (1) Imaging modality is specified (T2-weighted MRI). (2) Acquisition parameters are specified (TR=12,000ms, TE=156ms, flip angle=90°, SENSE factor, in-plane resolution 0.8mm × 0.8mm, slice thickness 1.6mm, overlap 0.8mm). nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: Neonatal MRI data were acquired on a Philips Achieva 3 Tesla system using a dedicated 32-channel neonatal head coil and positioning system at the Evelina Newborn Imaging Centre, Evelina London Children's Hospital (UK) as per (Hughes et al. 2017). Imaging was performed during natural sleep without sedation. T2-weighted scans were acquired with repetition time (TR)=12,000 ms, echo time (TE)=156 ms, flip angle=90°, SENSE factor=2.11/2.58 (axial/sagittal). The resultant in-plane resolution was 0.8 mm × 0.8 mm with a slice thickness of 1.6 mm and a slice overlap of 0.8 mm.

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: This study uses PRIMARY data collection for the clinical cohort (eBiDS study). All three criteria are satisfied: (1) Patient eligibility and diagnostic criteria are described - neonates with postnatally confirmed karyotype for DS, recruited from neonatal unit and postnatal wards, with scans up to <46 weeks PMA. (2) Image quality and data completeness standards are specified - same exclusion criteria as control group applied, with specific exclusion of acute brain infarction/parenchymal hemorrhage. (3) Final sample size (n=25) and reasons for exclusion are reported (10 excluded for old acquisition protocols, 1 excluded for acute brain infarction).
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: Neonates with a postnatally confirmed karyotype for DS were recruited from the neonatal unit and postnatal wards at St Thomas' Hospital London and invited for a neonatal scan up to < 46 weeks PMA at scan. Additionally, former fetal scan participants with a confirmed postnatal diagnosis of DS were invited for a neonatal scan if they had consented to be contacted post-delivery. A total of 36 neonates with DS were recruited to the T21 and eBiDS studies between 2014 and 2021. Ten neonatal scans were excluded from analysis due to the use of old acquisition protocols, which were not in line with the dHCP controls. One neonate was excluded from analysis due to an acute brain infarction/parenchymal hemorrhage. Therefore, data from 25 neonates with DS [12 female, 10 preterm births < 37 weeks GA, PMA at scan median (range) = 40.57 (32.43-45.57) weeks] (Table S1), scanned using the same acquisition parameters as dHCP controls, were used for analysis in this study.
